prompt:

Make that seam match Image 2: a very fine, restrained dark-walnut pixel boundary integrated into the wood, not a strong black cartoon outline.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact edit target. Image 2 is the approved bedroom and is the authority for the thickness and brown color of the wall-cap-to-void transition.
Allowed change: Recolor and thin only the outermost top wall-cap boundary against the black void, including the two diagonal runs and their short end returns. Use a single delicate stepped dark-brown line with subtle neighboring walnut pixels. Remove the visual impression of a thick black border while keeping the cap edge crisp.
Preserve exactly: every pixel-painted room element away from that top perimeter; exact 1774x887 canvas and fixed isometric composition; black surrounding void; wall-cap width and geometry; both doors; all walls; the already-corrected floor edge and full floor thickness; window, cabinets, sink, kettle, stove, refrigerator, plant, rug, table, chairs, laptops, papers, mugs, power strip, lighting, colors, and object positions. Keep all current hotspot geometry valid.
Constraints: Do not edit the lower/inner line beneath the wall cap unless required to match Image 2. Do not touch the floor perimeter. Do not move, redraw, add, or remove any object. No blur or antialiasing; retain crisp deliberate pixel clusters.
Avoid: black border bands, bold cartoon outlines, changed wall-cap thickness, altered room footprint, changed perspective, changed lighting, changed furniture, missing floor sides, smooth vector edges, characters, UI, text, logos, or watermark.
review: The outer top perimeter now uses a fine dark-walnut transition instead of the prior near-black band. Both diagonal wall-cap runs remain crisp and continuous.
